questions.question: What is the main claim of the first truth in this passage?
questions.answer: It teaches that true worship belongs only to Allah and that absolute divinity cannot be shared with anyone else.

questions.question: What kinds of worship in the universe are mentioned as signs of this truth?
questions.answer: The passage mentions human worship based on natural disposition, the function-based worship of living creatures and nonliving things, and the way blessings lead people to thank and praise Allah.

questions.question: How do blessings in the universe support the idea of worship?
questions.answer: They move people toward gratitude, praise, and thankfulness, which points them back to the One who gave those blessings.

questions.question: What unseen matters are said to support the exclusive right of Allah to be worshipped?
questions.answer: Spiritual disclosures, revelation, and inspiration are presented as agreeing that only Allah deserves worship.

questions.question: Why does the passage say divinity cannot accept any partner?
questions.answer: Because the conscious beings who worship are meant to turn to their real Lord, and if others could pull them away from Him, that would go against the very purpose of divinity.

questions.question: Who are described as the conscious and living fruits of the universe?
questions.answer: Human beings are described that way.

questions.question: Why might people be at risk of forgetting their true object of worship, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because Allah is unseen, so people may quickly become distracted and turn toward other things.

questions.question: What reason does the passage give for the Qur’an’s strong rejection of polytheism?
questions.answer: It rejects polytheism so strongly because associating partners with Allah clashes directly with the truth of absolute divinity.

questions.question: What can we infer about the relationship between gratitude and worship in this passage?
questions.answer: Gratitude is treated as part of worship because thanking for blessings should lead a person to the Giver.

questions.question: In one sentence, summarize how the whole universe points to one God in this passage.
questions.answer: The different forms of worship, the effect of blessings, and the witness of revelation and inspiration all come together to show that only Allah deserves worship.

questions.question: According to the passage, how does human nature relate to worship?
questions.answer: Human nature is described as leading different groups of people toward forms of worship suited to how they were created.

questions.question: How are animals and even nonliving things connected to worship in this passage?
questions.answer: Their carrying out of their built-in roles is presented as a kind of worship through obedience to what they were made to do.

questions.question: What effect do the gifts and favors in the universe have on people?
questions.answer: They encourage people to be thankful, to praise, and to worship.

questions.question: Which sources from beyond ordinary human observation are mentioned as supporting the truth of one God deserving worship?
questions.answer: The passage points to spiritual manifestations, revelation, and inspiration.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw from all these signs together?
questions.answer: It concludes that there is one absolute divinity ruling over all and that only Allah is fit to be worshipped.

questions.question: Why are human beings given special importance in the argument?
questions.answer: Because they are conscious, living beings and are presented as the highest fruits of creation who respond with worship and thanks.

questions.question: What problem would arise if others could attract people’s worship away from Allah?
questions.answer: That would defeat the purpose of divinity by misdirecting worship from its rightful goal.

questions.question: Why is Allah’s being unseen mentioned in the argument?
questions.answer: It explains why people can be vulnerable to forgetting Him if they let other things capture their attention.

questions.question: How does the passage connect polytheism with forgetting Allah?
questions.answer: It presents polytheism as a turning away from the true object of worship toward others.

questions.question: What attitude of the Qur’an toward polytheism is described?
questions.answer: The Qur’an is described as rejecting it repeatedly and forcefully and warning those who hold it.

questions.question: What is the strongest overall message a student should take from this passage?
questions.answer: Every true form of worship, gratitude, and spiritual testimony should direct a person to Allah alone, without assigning any partner to Him.

questions.question: What title is given to the truth explained in this target passage?
questions.answer: It is called absolute divinity.

questions.question: What evidence from human life is used to support this truth?
questions.answer: The passage uses the fact that different kinds of people are naturally drawn to worship in ways that fit their created nature.

questions.question: What evidence from the rest of creation is used besides human worship?
questions.answer: It points to the way living creatures and even nonliving things fulfill their essential tasks as a form of worship.

questions.question: How do worldly and spiritual blessings both support the same conclusion?
questions.answer: Material blessings lead to thankfulness, while spiritual signs like revelation and inspiration also testify that worship belongs only to Allah.

questions.question: What does the phrase “exclusive fitness” mean in this passage?
questions.answer: It means that only Allah is truly worthy of being worshipped.

questions.question: Why would shared divinity contradict the truth described here?
questions.answer: Because if worship could be rightfully directed to others, then absolute divinity would no longer be absolute.

questions.question: In the image used by the passage, where are conscious worshippers located in relation to the universe?
questions.answer: They are like the living, aware fruits found on the highest branches of a great tree.

questions.question: Why is it especially serious if those conscious beings are turned away from Allah?
questions.answer: Because they are the ones meant to respond with worship, thanks, and awareness, so their being misled damages the purpose of creation.

questions.question: What cause-and-effect relationship is described between receiving favors and worship?
questions.answer: Receiving blessings can make people feel grateful, and that gratitude should lead them to worship Allah.

questions.question: What can be inferred about shirk from the logic of the passage?
questions.answer: Shirk is not just a mistaken belief; it misdirects the deepest response of the human heart away from Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage explain the sharp language of the Qur’an against polytheism?
questions.answer: It explains that such language fits the seriousness of a belief that opposes the very nature of divinity.

questions.question: Give a brief summary of the argument in your own words.
questions.answer: The passage argues that all kinds of worship, blessings, and spiritual testimony point to Allah alone, so giving worship to anyone else goes against the truth of divinity.

questions.question: What truth is being proven in this passage through examples from the whole universe?
questions.answer: The truth being proven is that there is one absolute divinity and that worship belongs only to Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the worship done by different groups of people?
questions.answer: It says their worship follows their natural disposition.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the activities of creatures and even lifeless things?
questions.answer: Their fulfilling their essential roles is treated as a kind of worship.

questions.question: How do gifts in the universe function in the argument?
questions.answer: They act as reasons for people to thank, praise, and worship Allah.

questions.question: Which higher forms of guidance are mentioned as agreeing on this truth?
questions.answer: Revelation, inspiration, and spiritual unveilings are mentioned.

questions.question: What does the agreement of all these signs show?
questions.answer: It shows in a strong and clear way that only one God is worthy of worship.

questions.question: Why does the passage focus on conscious and living beings when discussing worship?
questions.answer: Because they can knowingly respond to blessings with thanks and devotion.

questions.question: What danger is described if other beings are seen as the real source of what people receive?
questions.answer: People may feel bound to those beings and direct their worship away from Allah.

questions.question: Why would that danger be completely opposed to divinity?
questions.answer: Because divinity requires that worship reach its true and only rightful object.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about the purpose of human thankfulness?
questions.answer: Its purpose is to return to Allah through worship and recognition of His favors.

questions.question: How does the passage connect belief and consequences when speaking about polytheists?
questions.answer: It says the Qur’an both strongly refutes their belief and warns them of punishment.

questions.question: What lesson should a Muslim student draw from this passage about daily life?
questions.answer: Every blessing and every moment of gratitude should remind us to worship Allah alone and guard ourselves from giving His rights to anything else.

questions.question: What is the central teaching of “Absolute Divinity” in this passage?
questions.answer: The central teaching is that Allah alone deserves worship and that no partner can share in His divinity.

questions.question: Name three types of evidence used to support that teaching.
questions.answer: The passage uses human worship, the obedient functioning of creatures and things, and spiritual testimony such as revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: How are ordinary blessings connected to belief in one God here?
questions.answer: They are described as pushing people toward thankfulness and praise, which should lead to worship of Allah.

questions.question: What idea about the entire cosmos is implied by the examples in the passage?
questions.answer: The whole universe is shown as directing attention toward the worship of one Lord.

questions.question: According to the passage, who are the highest responders to divinity?
questions.answer: Conscious and living beings, especially human beings, are the highest responders.

questions.question: Why is their response so important in the argument?
questions.answer: Because they are the ones who can knowingly give thanks and worship, so where they direct that worship matters greatly.

questions.question: What would be wrong with others making people feel obligated to them in a way that replaces worship of Allah?
questions.answer: It would pull worship away from its rightful place and oppose the sacred aim of divinity.

questions.question: What human weakness does the passage hint at when it says the true object of worship may be quickly forgotten?
questions.answer: It hints that people can become distracted by visible things and neglect Allah, who is unseen.

questions.question: What does the repeated Qur’anic rejection of polytheism show about its seriousness?
questions.answer: It shows that polytheism is a major violation of the truth that belongs at the center of faith.

questions.question: State the passage’s message in one clear sentence for an 11th-grade student.
questions.answer: Everything that leads us to worship, thank, and praise should bring us to Allah alone, because sharing His worship with others is false.

questions.question: What does the passage try to prove by mentioning worship throughout creation?
questions.answer: It tries to prove that there is one absolute divinity and that Allah alone is worthy of worship.

questions.question: How is worship shown in human beings according to the passage?
questions.answer: It is shown through forms of devotion that fit the natural way people were created.

questions.question: How is worship shown in nonhuman creation?
questions.answer: It appears in the way animals and even lifeless things carry out the roles given to them.

questions.question: What role do blessings and gifts play in the argument?
questions.answer: They stir people to gratitude, praise, and worship, pointing them to Allah.

questions.question: What spiritual sources are said to confirm this truth?
questions.answer: The passage says revelation, inspiration, and spiritual manifestations confirm it.

questions.question: What overall judgment does the passage make after listing these signs?
questions.answer: It judges that they clearly establish the reality and supremacy of one divinity.

questions.question: Why can absolute divinity not be shared with anyone else?
questions.answer: Because the right to be worshipped belongs fully to Allah, and sharing it would contradict the nature of divinity itself.

questions.question: Why are conscious beings described in such an honored position within creation?
questions.answer: Because they are able to recognize blessings and answer with worship and thanks.

questions.question: What mistaken shift does the passage warn against?
questions.answer: It warns against turning people’s devotion away from Allah and toward other beings.

questions.question: How does the passage explain the spiritual harm of that shift?
questions.answer: It breaks the proper relationship between the worshipper and the One who truly deserves worship.

questions.question: Why is the Qur’an’s warning about Hell mentioned at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: It emphasizes how seriously Islam treats associating partners with Allah.

questions.question: What is one practical way this passage can shape a Muslim teenager’s mindset?
questions.answer: It can teach a Muslim teenager to see every blessing as a reason to thank Allah first and to protect the heart from any form of shirk.
